description: Roll up order revenue per store per LOCAL business day. order_ts is stored in UTC; each store has an IANA timezone name. The local day is the calendar date of order_ts converted to the store's timezone, honoring daylight saving time transitions. Output columns: store_id (INT64), local_date (DATE), revenue (FLOAT64), order_count (INT64). Sort by store_id, local_date.

utc_offset_hours.description: DEPRECATED static standard-time offset; do not use

edge_cases: 2025-03-09 is the US DST start: order 3 at 06:59Z on March 10 is 23:59 PDT on March 9 (UTC-7), not March 10
Order 1 at 07:30Z is 23:30 PST on March 8 (UTC-8, before the switch)
Tokyo order at 15:00Z falls on the next local day
Stores in different timezones can map the same UTC instant to different local dates
common_failure_modes: FM2: DATE(order_ts) in UTC assigns orders 1, 3 and 4 to the wrong day
FM2: Applying the static utc_offset_hours (-8) ignores DST: after the switch every order between 07:00Z and 08:00Z is assigned to the previous local day, a one-hour drift for half the year
FM4: DATE(order_ts, timezone) accepts a per-row timezone column in BigQuery; TIMESTAMP_SUB with a constant interval does not model DST
